title: Rolling 12-week burn cadence and skill-lift sensitivity scan
content:
Executive summary:

This workbook models a 12-week rolling burn cadence paired with a skills-focused hiring ladder. Purpose: give product & platform leaders a short-horizon decision tool that answers: if we accelerate / pause hiring and if price/margin moves by +/- 15%, how does cash consumption and SLA-sensitive capacity change over the quarter?

Key takeaways (top-level):
- Baseline (status quo hires + current pricing): runway impact over 12w = -12.4% of current cash cadence; weekly burn average = $2.05M.
- Fast-hire (+6 FTEs concentrated in infra + SRE in weeks 2-6) reduces operational risk but increases 12w burn by 9.7% (peak weekly burn +14%).
- Skill-lift (shift 4 hires from junior -> mid-level with higher ramp) increases near-term cash but shortens time-to-productivity — by week 10 expected throughput improvement lowers unit cost for hosted API routes by ~4.2%.
- Price compression sensitivity: -15% effective per-token price (market pressure) increases 12w cash out by ~7.9% under baseline usage; combining fast-hire and -15% price results in worst-case 18% increase to rolling burn.

Assumptions (model inputs):
- Starting cash: $220M.
- Current weekly op-ex (non-headcount): $350k (licenses, cloud egress, storage).
- Current headcount cost (cash burn) baseline: $8.2M / quarter = $2.05M / week. This includes payroll + benefits + recruiting burn allocated.
- Hiring plan: baseline adds 3 FTEs (2 eng infra, 1 product ops) spread weeks 3-9; fast-hire adds 6 FTEs (4 infra, 2 SRE) weeks 2-6. Role ramp profiles: junior ramp 26w to full productivity (0.25 linear first 12w), mid ramp 16w (0.5 linear first 12w).
- Typical new-hire cash impact: sign + first-month cost = 1.25x monthly salary; thereafter 1.0x. Average FTE fully-loaded cost: junior $18k/mo, mid $29k/mo, senior $45k/mo.
- Dedicated capacity and GPU commitments: incremental $120k/week at high-utilization reserve levels when we enable burst pools for Dedicated customers; assumed triggered in scenario where committed throughput > 85% for two consecutive weeks.
- Pricing sensitivity modeled as uniform percent change to per-token revenue for hosted routes.

Notes on table: numbers above show blended headcount cash assuming fast-hire scenario triggered in weeks 2-6 and GPU reserve for Dedicated briefly active for weeks 2-6. Baseline lane (no fast-hire, no GPU reserve) averages $2.05M/week HC + $350k non-HC => $2.4M/week.

Headcount ladder (role, count, avg fully-loaded monthly cost, ramp weeks to 0.5 productivity, cash delta vs junior)
Junior Eng | 12 | $18,000 | 26 | baseline
Mid Eng | 8  | $29,000 | 16 | +$11,000/mo per role
SRE (mid)  | 4  | $33,000 | 12 | +$15,000/mo per role
Infra (senior) | 3 | $45,000 | 8 | +$27,000/mo per role
Product Ops (mid) | 2 | $28,000 | 12 | +$10,000/mo per role

Skill-lift tradeoffs (quantified):
- Replace 4 junior hires with 4 mid hires (same hire count), immediate 12-week cash delta: +$44k/week across the 12w window (higher salaries + sign-on), but expected reduction in external GPU/reserve triggers because productivity rises: estimated 12w avoided GPU spend = $420k => net cash delta by week 12 = +$88k (small net increase) but lowers downstream unit cost by ~3.9% by week 16.

Sensitivity scenarios (concise):
1) Baseline pricing + baseline hiring: 12w total burn = $31.1M. Runway delta: -5.6 weeks vs static headcount freeze.
2) -15% pricing + baseline hiring: 12w total burn = $33.6M (+8.0%). Primary driver: revenue down, customer mix static.
3) -15% pricing + fast-hire: 12w total burn = $36.7M (+18.1% vs baseline). Worst near-term cash case.
4) Price +10% (favorable) + skill-lift hires: 12w total burn = $29.4M (-5.5% from baseline) because higher margins offset incremental HC.

Trigger rules (operational):
- If committed throughput > 85% for 2w => enable Dedicated burst pool (inject $120k/wk) and accelerate hiring to reduce risk. Finance must approve an emergency reserve draw >= $1.2M for capacity spikes.
- If rolling 4-week realized revenue falls > 8% YoY => freeze external hiring for 6 weeks, re-evaluate price buckets.

Recommendations (actionable):
- Short horizon (next 12w): prioritize skill-lift hires over pure headcount increases for customer-facing infra routes that show persistent 75-90% utilization. This reduces downstream GPU reserve risk and improves unit economics.
- Mid horizon (12-26w): build a small $2.5M buffer specifically earmarked for Dedicated burst commits to avoid last-minute expensive capacity purchases.
- Pricing: prepare a staged defensive price action (volume concessions for mid-market) to limit per-token price erosion to <10% while protecting enterprise ARPU via tiered commitments.

Open questions & data needs:
- Need route-level unit economics for top 20 customers by token-volume (currently aggregated at product line level).
- Better estimate of sign-on timing (actual offer to payroll date) — recruiting currently averages 5.6 weeks, but hiring-sim assumes 3 weeks for fast-hire.
- Quantify elasticity: how much usage would we recover if we raised price by +5% on non-committed tiers? (basic elasticity study requested).

Appendix (formulas & small model notes):
- New hire cash step-up = pro-rated monthly salary * ramp fraction + sign-on uplift.
- Ramp productivity assumed linear unless otherwise noted.
- GPU reserve trigger logic in model uses 7-day rolling average of committed qps and expected per-request token consumption.

Version history:
- 2025-10-15 initial draft by Asha Patel (baseline model)
- 2025-11-02 added skill-lift scenario (Marta)
- 2026-01-28 integrated fast-hire and Dedicated reserve triggers (Liam)
- 2026-02-04 sensitivity re-run with price compression bands (Asha)

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Product/Eng: deliver route-level token mix by 2026-02-18 (owner: Ethan Brooks).
- Recruiting: validate 2-week acceleration feasibility for targeted mid hires by 2026-02-12 (owner: Marta Ruiz).
- Finance: convert model to a linked sheet with dynamic sliders for price %, hire cadence, and GPU reserve cost by 2026-02-11 (owner: Asha Patel).

Notes to reviewer: this is a short-horizon working sheet. Numbers intentionally conservative on efficiency gains; if route-level metrics show higher CPU/GPU efficiencies we should re-run upside scenarios.
